title: Starter Acculturation: 36hr Technical Quiet Bootcamp
summary: A compact, low-interruption 36-hour onboarding playbook created for technical hires and short-term contractors who benefit from a "quiet launch" (minimal meetings, focused setup tasks, and early signal-of-success activities). Balances access priorities, early contributor work that yields a visible ship, and manager/mentor responsibilities to reduce cognitive load and accelerate useful output.
body:
Purpose:
This is a tactical checklist and schedule for the first 36 hours after an engineer (FTE or contract) accepts an offer and completes initial provisioning. It’s designed for contributors who need an asynchronous, low-meeting ramp so they can productively touch code, tests, infra, or documentation within 36 hours while still getting essential social/contextual onboarding.

Intended audience:
- New technical hire / contractor
- Hiring manager
- Assigned mentor (peer buddy)
- People Ops coordinator

Core principles:
1) Minimum friction to run real tasks: prioritize access to a single micro-feature or fix that exercises CI, repo, and infra.
2) Fewer synchronous meetings: keep calendar < 2 hours in first 36 hours.
3) Early visible signal: ship a small change that can be reviewed and merged so the new hire experiences the full loop.
4) Psychological safety: checklists, templates, and a single point of contact for early blockers.

Preboarding (before day 0, People Ops):
- Send the "36hr-quiet-launch packet" with links and a one-line success goal (e.g., "Open a PR that fixes a lint error and passes CI").
- Provision accounts in priority order (GitHub, email, Slack, VPN/KMS access if needed, CI runner debug access). Mark what still pending and who the owner is.
- Create a single onboarding GitHub issue (title: "36hr-bootcamp: <name> - first task") with checklist and assignment to mentor.

Day 0 (arrival window ~hour 0):
- Automated welcome email (template included below).
- Manager 15-min sync (optional asynchronous note if manager busy) covering: one-sentence team mission, the 36-hr success goal, and contact policy.
- Mentor pings on Slack channel + shares the onboarding issue link.
- New hire sanity-check of access list (yes/no answers for each system) submitted to People Ops thread.

36hr schedule (recommended cadence):
Hour 0–2: orientation + access verification
- Read the 10-min team README (link in packet).
- Confirm GitHub access: clone repo, run local lint/test script. Record output in the onboarding issue.
- If blocked, add details to the issue and tag mentor.

Hour 2–12: focused task and small exploratory work
- Pick the micro-task in the onboarding issue (examples: fix failing lint, small doc update, a unit test, or a tiny config change).
- Work privately and push an initial branch. Encourage small, frequent commits.

Hour 12–24: PR cycle and CI feedback
- Open PR with clear title/summary and link to onboarding issue.
- Mentor reviews asynchronously; manager gets notified only if PR is blocked beyond 12 hours.
- Address CI failures; if infra-related, escalate to the SRE oncall (contact info in packet).

Hour 24–36: merge + post-merge check + 36hr retro
- Merge PR if passing and has approvals (follow team merge rules).
- Run any post-merge smoke tests (local or staging) and log results in the issue.
- New hire writes a 5–7 sentence "first-36hr" note: what they learned, blockers, and what they'd like next. Add to the issue and ping manager.

Manager responsibilities (concise):
- Approve the core success goal and ensure it’s realistic for the role.
- Reserve a 15-min window within first 4 hours for a check-in (recorded as optional).
- Assign and introduce an explicit mentor (not the manager) and ensure the mentor has < 2 hrs blocked in their calendar for the period.
- Triage any policy/security block within 6 hours with People Ops or Security.

Mentor checklist (first 36 hours):
- Send Slack DM with onboarding issue link and the quick-start runbook.
- Be reachable asynchronously (within 60–90 minutes) for clarifying questions.
- Provide PR feedback with actionable comments; encourage small scope.
- At 36 hours, leave a closing comment with recommended next tasks and learning resources.

People Ops checklist (coordination role):
- Confirm identity and KYC steps (if required) before day 0.
- Ensure hardware shipping tracking is shared if applicable.
- Maintain the access matrix and escalate any missing entries within business hours.

Example welcome email (send automatically on day 0):
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — 36hr Quiet Launch Packet
Hi <name>,
Welcome! We’ve set a lean first task to get you into the repo and CI loop quickly. Your 36hr success goal: "Open a PR that exercises our CI and results in a merged change or documented blocker."
Links: team README | onboarding issue | mentor Slack DM
If anything is blocked, reply to this email and tag @people-ops. We’ll escalate.
Cheers,
People Ops

Templates (short):
- GitHub Issue title: "36hr-bootcamp: <name> - first task"
- PR description header: "What: (1–2 lines)
Why: (context)
How to test: (steps)"

Acceptance signals (how we know 36 hours worked):
- Primary: PR opened and merged (or a clear blocker documented and triaged).
- Secondary: New hire ran local test/lint and reported status in onboarding issue.
- Tertiary: New hire posted the 5–7 sentence retro in the issue and identified next 1–2 learning tasks.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Access delay > 6 hours: People Ops escalation and temporary guest access to required CI.
- CI infra flakiness: Mentor files a quick SRE ticket and tags the oncall. People Ops notes the incident to improve the next packet.
- New hire overwhelmed: pause the bootcamp, schedule a 30-min human sync, and convert to a 5-day light ramp.

Notes to the program owner (People Ops):
- Track 36-hr success rates weekly per hiring source (contractor vs FTE) and surface recurrent blockers (e.g., VPN provisioning).
- Maintain a small catalog of micro-tasks per repo to avoid hunting overhead.
- Consider a Slack automation that pings the mentor if no PR within 18 hours.

Open questions (for design review):
- Should manager always require an explicit present-or-absent 15-min sync, or allow opt-out for very senior ICs?
- What is the maximum acceptable fraction of hires that convert this 36-hr plan to a slower 5-day ramp? (propose <= 25%)

Appendix: Quick access priority (order)
1) GitHub org access (clone/push/PR)
2) Slack and team channel (read + DM)
3) Email + company calendar
4) VPN / KMS / secret-reader for infra work
5) CI runner debug permissions (if relevant)

This doc is intentionally prescriptive and minimal — treat it as an option for teams that value early independent momentum and low-calendar onboarding. Track results in JIRA:PEOPLE-482 and iterate quarterly.
